She sought treatment because of numbness in her left lower limb and difficulty playing softball. Despite conservative treatment for a year, her symptoms did not improve. Physical examination revealed decreased left patellar tendon reflexes and numbness and pain from the front of the left thigh to the lower leg without muscle weakness. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Sagittal CT directly visualizes bilateral L5 pars interarticularis defects (the pathognomonic isthmic lesion); caption and in-text evidence both identify this specific manifestation and the article is disease-focused. B: Axial CT shows the pars interarticularis defects (gaps) at L5, the defining isthmic spondylolysis lesion, directly supported by caption and in-text evidence. C: MRI shows exiting L5 nerve root compression at the L4/L5 foramen, a vocabulary-listed manifestation of isthmic spondylolisthesis in this patient with documented L5 spondylolysis; attribution is slightly weaker because the compression is attributed to a superior-level disc protrusion rather than the pars lesion itself.
